response.sql:
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT invoice_number,
         AVG(derived_product_cost) AS avg_cost,
         SUM(derived_total_cost) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(product_price), 0) AS ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM inv WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT AVG(i.avg_cost) AS avg_line_product_cost,
       AVG(i.ratio) AS avg_ratio,
       AVG(i.ratio) - o.avg_ratio AS ratio_excess_over_overall_avg
FROM inv i
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE i.ratio > o.avg_ratio
GROUP BY o.avg_ratio;

assumptions.assumption: Each invoice's ratio is SUM(derived_total_cost) / SUM(product_price), with SQL SUM ignoring NULLs independently in numerator and denominator. Invoices whose price sum is NULL or 0 have no ratio. They are excluded from the overall average and from the kept set.

An invoice's average line product cost is AVG(derived_product_cost) over its lines with a non-NULL value. The 'overall average ratio' is the unweighted mean of invoice ratios, not a ratio of grand totals.

alternatives.interpretation: A line counts toward an invoice's ratio only if both derived_total_cost and product_price are non-NULL, so the numerator and denominator cover the same lines.
alternatives.sql:
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT invoice_number,
         AVG(derived_product_cost) AS avg_cost,
         SUM(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND product_price IS NOT NULL THEN derived_total_cost END) * 1.0
           / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND product_price IS NOT NULL THEN product_price END), 0) AS ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM inv WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT AVG(i.avg_cost) AS avg_line_product_cost,
       AVG(i.ratio) AS avg_ratio,
       AVG(i.ratio) - o.avg_ratio AS ratio_excess_over_overall_avg
FROM inv i
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE i.ratio > o.avg_ratio
GROUP BY o.avg_ratio;
